title: Acts Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Acts 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The priests, and the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them
Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander gathered at Jerusalem
Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, spoke to the rulers
Many of those who heard the word believed
questions.correctAnswer: The priests, and the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them
questions.explanation: Acts 4:1 states that the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them as they spoke to the people, which is the earliest event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: Who came upon the apostles as they spoke unto the people in Acts 4?
options: The priests, and the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees
The rulers, and elders, and scribes
Annas the high priest and Caiaphas
questions.correctAnswer: The priests, and the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees
questions.explanation: Acts 4:1 states that the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them as they spoke unto the people.

questions.question: Why were the priests and Sadducees grieved according to Acts 4?
options: Because they taught the people, and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead
Because they healed the impotent man
Because they spoke against the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Because they taught the people, and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead
questions.explanation: Acts 4:2 states that the priests and Sadducees were grieved that the apostles taught the people and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead.

questions.question: What did the authorities do to the apostles after laying hands on them in Acts 4?
options: Put them in hold unto the next day
questions.correctAnswer: Put them in hold unto the next day
questions.explanation: Acts 4:3 states that the authorities laid hands on the apostles and put them in hold until the next day.

questions.question: Approximately how many men believed after hearing the word in Acts 4?
questions.correctAnswer: About five thousand
questions.explanation: Acts 4:4 states that many who heard the word believed, and the number of the men was about five thousand.

questions.question: Who gathered together at Jerusalem on the morrow according to Acts 4?
options: The priests and the captain of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Their rulers, elders, and scribes
questions.explanation: Acts 4:5 states that on the morrow, their rulers, elders, and scribes gathered together.

questions.question: Which high priests are mentioned as gathered together in Acts 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Annas and Caiaphas
questions.explanation: Acts 4:6 mentions Annas the high priest and Caiaphas among those gathered together at Jerusalem.

questions.question: What question did the rulers ask Peter and John in Acts 4?
options: By what power, or by what name, have ye done this?
Where did you get this man's healing power?
Who told you to teach the people?
Why do you preach Jesus in the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: By what power, or by what name, have ye done this?
questions.explanation: Acts 4:7 states that the rulers asked Peter and John by what power or by what name they did the miracle.

questions.question: Who spoke to the rulers and elders filled with the Holy Ghost in Acts 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Peter
questions.explanation: Acts 4:8 states that Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, spoke to the rulers and elders of Israel.

questions.question: By what name did Peter say the impotent man was made whole in Acts 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus Christ of Nazareth
questions.explanation: Acts 4:10 states that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth the man stands whole before them.

questions.question: What is said about the stone in Acts 4?
options: It was set at nought by the builders and has become the head of the corner
It was the foundation of the temple
It was a symbol of the law
It was used to build the city gates
questions.correctAnswer: It was set at nought by the builders and has become the head of the corner
questions.explanation: Acts 4:11 says this is the stone which was set at nought of the builders, which is become the head of the corner.

questions.question: According to Acts 4, is there salvation in any other name besides Jesus?
options: No, there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved
Only through the name of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: No, there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved
questions.explanation: Acts 4:12 states explicitly that there is no salvation in any other name than Jesus.

questions.question: What did the rulers perceive about Peter and John in Acts 4?
options: That they were unlearned and ignorant men
That they were highly educated scribes
questions.correctAnswer: That they were unlearned and ignorant men
questions.explanation: Acts 4:13 says the rulers perceived that Peter and John were unlearned and ignorant men.

questions.question: True or False: The number of men who believed after hearing the word was about five thousand.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 4:4 states many who heard the word believed, and the number of the men was about five thousand.

questions.question: True or False: Peter was filled with the Holy Ghost when he spoke to the rulers and elders.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 4:8 states that Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, spoke to the rulers and elders of Israel.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the rulers and elders say they could not deny?
options: A notable miracle hath been done
questions.correctAnswer: A notable miracle hath been done
questions.explanation: This is found in Acts 4:16, where the rulers acknowledge the miracle done by Peter and John.

questions.question: What does Acts 4:18 promise will happen if someone does not teach in the name of Jesus?
questions.correctAnswer: They will face punishment
questions.explanation: Acts 4:18 shows that they commanded Peter and John not to speak or teach in the name of Jesus, implying consequences for disobedience.

questions.question: What did Peter and John assert about speaking of what they had seen and heard?
questions.correctAnswer: They cannot but speak
questions.explanation: Acts 4:20 states that they cannot stop speaking about what they have seen and heard, emphasizing their commitment to their testimony.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people when Peter and John were threatened?
options: They glorified God for the miracle
They turned against Peter and John
questions.correctAnswer: They glorified God for the miracle
questions.explanation: Acts 4:21 indicates that the people glorified God for the healing, which influenced the rulers' decision to let Peter and John go.

questions.question: How old was the man who was healed?
questions.correctAnswer: Above 40 years old
questions.explanation: Acts 4:22 clearly states that the man was above forty years old when the miracle of healing was shown to him.

questions.question: What did Peter and John do after being released from the council?
options: They reported to their own company
They went back to the temple to preach
questions.correctAnswer: They reported to their own company
questions.explanation: Acts 4:23 states that after being let go, they went to their own company and reported all that had been said to them.

questions.question: What did the disciples do after hearing about the threats?
questions.correctAnswer: They prayed with one accord
questions.explanation: Acts 4:24 shows that they lifted their voice to God with one accord, indicating unity in prayer in response to the threats.

questions.question: According to Acts 4:25, who spoke about the heathen raging?
questions.correctAnswer: David
questions.explanation: Acts 4:25 identifies David as the servant whose mouth spoke about why the heathen rage, connecting the early church's experiences with scripture.

questions.question: What does Acts 4:19 imply about the authority of God versus human authority?
options: God's authority must always be obeyed
questions.correctAnswer: God's authority must always be obeyed
questions.explanation: Acts 4:19 reveals Peter and John's stance that they must judge whether it is right to hearken to human authority over God's, emphasizing God's higher authority.

questions.question: What notable event prompted the council to take action against Peter and John?
options: The healing of the impotent man
questions.correctAnswer: The healing of the impotent man
questions.explanation: Acts 4:9-10 indicates that the council took action specifically because of the good deed done to the impotent man, which was a significant miracle.

questions.question: Why did the council decide to threaten Peter and John?
options: To stop the preaching of the resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: To protect their authority
questions.explanation: Acts 4:17 indicates that the council threatened Peter and John in order to prevent the spread of the miracle and maintain control over the people.

questions.question: The statement that Peter and John were unlearned and ignorant men is found in which verse?
questions.correctAnswer: Acts 4:13
questions.explanation: Acts 4:13 describes Peter and John as unlearned and ignorant men, yet they were bold and recognized for having been with Jesus.

questions.question: True or False: The council found a way to punish Peter and John.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 4:21 states that they found nothing how they might punish them, indicating that they could not act against Peter and John.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples were afraid and stopped preaching after being threatened.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 4:20 shows that Peter and John committed to speaking about what they had seen and heard, not halting their preaching.

questions.question: True or False: The name of Jesus was not mentioned during the council's questioning.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 4:10 specifically mentions that the miracle was done by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, indicating its importance in the discussion.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 4.

questions.question: According to Acts 4:27, which figures were gathered together against Jesus?
options: Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the people of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the people of Israel
questions.explanation: Acts 4:27 explicitly states that Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the people of Israel were gathered together against Jesus.

questions.question: What was the reason given in Acts 4:28 for the actions taken against Jesus?
options: Because it was determined by God's hand and counsel before to be done
Because of the envy of the chief priests
Because of fear of Roman authority
Because Jesus claimed to be king of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: Because it was determined by God's hand and counsel before to be done
questions.explanation: Acts 4:28 states that the actions against Jesus were done 'whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done,' indicating divine foreordination.

questions.question: In Acts 4:29, what do the apostles ask the Lord to grant them?
options: That with all boldness they may speak thy word
That they may be protected from their enemies
That they may receive wisdom to answer their opponents
questions.correctAnswer: That with all boldness they may speak thy word
questions.explanation: Acts 4:29 shows the apostles praying for boldness to speak God's word despite threats.

questions.question: What signs do the apostles pray to be done by the name of Jesus according to Acts 4:30?
options: Casting out demons and raising the dead
Feeding the multitudes and walking on water
questions.correctAnswer: Healing and wonders
questions.explanation: The verse Acts 4:30 specifically mentions 'by stretching forth thine hand to heal; and that signs and wonders may be done by the name of thy holy child Jesus.'

questions.question: What happened when the believers prayed in Acts 4:31?
options: The place was shaken, they were filled with the Holy Ghost, and spoke boldly
An angel appeared and reassured them
Their enemies were struck with fear
They received visions of the future
questions.correctAnswer: The place was shaken, they were filled with the Holy Ghost, and spoke boldly
questions.explanation: Acts 4:31 records that after prayer, 'the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness.'

questions.question: According to Acts 4:32, how were the believers described in terms of their possessions?
options: They had all things common and no one claimed private ownership
They kept their possessions private and guarded
They shared only food but not houses or lands
They sold everything and lived in poverty
questions.correctAnswer: They had all things common and no one claimed private ownership
questions.explanation: Acts 4:32 says the believers were 'of one heart and of one soul' and 'neither said any of them that ought of the things which he possessed was his own; but they had all things common.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'boldness' (Acts 4:29) mean in its original context?
questions.correctAnswer: Confidence and courage in speech
questions.explanation: The Greek word used here (παρρησία, parrēsía) means confidence or courage in speaking openly, as used in Acts 4:29.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Acts 4:27-28 to emphasize divine sovereignty?
options: Inclusio framing the prayer with divine control
Irony in the gathering of enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the prayer with divine control
questions.explanation: Acts 4:27-28 uses inclusio, framing the prayer by highlighting that though enemies gathered, it was according to God's predetermined plan, emphasizing divine sovereignty.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed in the prayer of Acts 4:25-26 regarding the raging of the heathen?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 2
questions.explanation: Acts 4:25-26 quotes Psalm 2, which speaks of the heathen raging and the kings conspiring against the Lord and His anointed.

questions.question: The apostles' boldness in Acts 4:13 is surprising because they were seen as:
questions.correctAnswer: Unlearned and ignorant men
questions.explanation: Acts 4:13 notes that the rulers marveled at the apostles' boldness since they were 'unlearned and ignorant men,' yet had been with Jesus.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the prayer in Acts 4:31?
options: The healing of a lame man
The selling of land and possessions
questions.correctAnswer: The prayer recorded in Acts 4:29-30
questions.explanation: Acts 4:31 follows directly after the prayer in verses 29-30 where the believers ask for boldness and for signs and wonders to be done.

questions.question: What typology is seen in the sharing of possessions among believers in Acts 4:32-35?
options: Foreshadowing the communal life of the early Church as a fulfillment of God's kingdom
A prophetic symbol of the Temple sacrifices
An allegory for the Exodus journey
A metaphor for spiritual gifts distribution
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing the communal life of the early Church as a fulfillment of God's kingdom
questions.explanation: Acts 4:32-35 depicts believers having all things common, which foreshadows the ideal communal life in God's kingdom and manifests the unity of the early Church.

questions.question: How does the apostles' witness in Acts 4:33 relate to the resurrection of Jesus?
options: They gave witness with great power of the resurrection
They denied the resurrection under threat
They ignored the resurrection in their teachings
They only spoke of Jesus' teachings, not resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: They gave witness with great power of the resurrection
questions.explanation: Acts 4:33 states the apostles gave witness with great power of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, demonstrating the centrality of this event in their testimony.

questions.question: Which historical-cultural context does the sale of land by Barnabas in Acts 4:37 illustrate?
options: The early Christian practice of voluntary communal sharing
questions.correctAnswer: The early Christian practice of voluntary communal sharing
questions.explanation: Acts 4:37 shows Barnabas selling land and bringing the money to the apostles, illustrating voluntary communal sharing characteristic of the early Church.

questions.question: The phrase 'with one accord' in Acts 4:24 is an example of which literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism emphasizing unity
questions.explanation: Acts 4:24 uses 'with one accord' to emphasize unity among the believers, a form of parallelism common in Hebrew prayer and poetry.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 4:12 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is found exclusively in Jesus Christ
Salvation can be attained through good deeds
Salvation is available through multiple religious names
Salvation depends on human wisdom and effort
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is found exclusively in Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Acts 4:12 states 'Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved,' affirming salvation is only through Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine about the Holy Spirit is taught in Acts 4:8?
options: The Holy Spirit empowers believers to witness boldly
The Holy Spirit is limited in guiding speech
The Holy Spirit only works through miracles
The Holy Spirit is not involved in apostolic ministry
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit empowers believers to witness boldly
questions.explanation: Acts 4:8 says that Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, spoke boldly to the rulers and elders, showing the Spirit's role in empowering witness.

questions.question: What doctrine about the community of believers is taught in Acts 4:32?
options: Believers share all possessions in common as an expression of unity
Believers are commanded to separate materially
Believers are indifferent to material needs
questions.correctAnswer: Believers share all possessions in common as an expression of unity
questions.explanation: Acts 4:32 describes the believers as being 'of one heart and of one soul' and having 'all things common,' teaching the doctrine of communal sharing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 4:28 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Acts 4:28 speaks of God's hand and counsel determining events beforehand, demonstrating God's sovereignty over history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Acts 4:24 when the believers praise God as maker of heaven and earth?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Acts 4:24 acknowledges God as creator of all things, emphasizing His omnipotence.

questions.question: How does Acts 4:10 connect with Old Testament Messianic prophecy?
options: It identifies Jesus as the rejected stone becoming the cornerstone
It denies the fulfillment of any prophecy in Jesus
It presents Jesus only as a moral teacher
It equates Jesus with an Old Testament priest
questions.correctAnswer: It identifies Jesus as the rejected stone becoming the cornerstone
questions.explanation: Acts 4:10-11 references the stone rejected by builders becoming the head of the corner, fulfilling Psalm 118:22 as a Messianic prophecy.

questions.question: In what way does the communal sharing in Acts 4:34-35 fulfill the ethical teachings of the early church in Acts 2?
options: It continues the demonstrated love and unity among believers
It contradicts the individual ownership emphasized earlier
It introduces a new legalistic requirement
It focuses exclusively on clergy possessions
questions.correctAnswer: It continues the demonstrated love and unity among believers
questions.explanation: Acts 4:34-35 shows believers selling property to meet needs, echoing the unity and sharing seen in Acts 2:44-45.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 4:19 and Acts 4:20 teach about obedience and witness?
options: Obedience to God supersedes human authority in proclaiming the gospel
Human authority must be obeyed over divine commands
Witness is optional and can be silenced by threats
Obedience to human rulers is the highest priority
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God supersedes human authority in proclaiming the gospel
questions.explanation: Acts 4:19-20 shows Peter and John refusing to obey human prohibitions against speaking in Jesus' name, prioritizing obedience to God.

questions.question: What combined teaching about prayer and boldness is found in Acts 4:29-31?
options: Prayer empowers bold proclamation of God's word despite opposition
Boldness comes from human courage alone
Prayer should avoid mention of opposition
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer empowers bold proclamation of God's word despite opposition
questions.explanation: Acts 4:29-31 records prayer for boldness and the subsequent filling with the Holy Spirit enabling fearless preaching.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal theme about Jesus' resurrection and healing ministry is taught in Acts 4:9-10 and Acts 4:30?
options: Jesus’ resurrection authority enables healing and confirms His messianic identity
Healing is independent of Jesus’ resurrection
Resurrection and healing are unrelated events
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ resurrection authority enables healing and confirms His messianic identity
questions.explanation: Acts 4:9-10 and 4:30 link Jesus’ resurrection and the healing signs done in His name, affirming His divine authority.

questions.question: Skeptics claim the apostles’ boldness was merely human confidence. What does Acts 4:7-8 actually teach about the source of their boldness?
options: Their boldness is the result of being filled with the Holy Ghost
Their boldness was due to political influence
Their boldness came from their education
Their boldness was a natural personality trait
questions.correctAnswer: Their boldness is the result of being filled with the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Acts 4:7-8 explicitly states Peter was 'filled with the Holy Ghost' before boldly speaking, indicating divine empowerment.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the nature of the early church's unity is taught in Acts 4:32 and Acts 4:33?
options: Unity is both spiritual and practical, empowered by the Holy Spirit’s power
Unity is only social with no spiritual basis
Unity is enforced by legalistic rules
questions.correctAnswer: Unity is both spiritual and practical, empowered by the Holy Spirit’s power
questions.explanation: Acts 4:32-33 shows believers united in heart and soul, sharing possessions, and empowered by the Holy Spirit to witness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Acts 4:27-28 regarding the fulfillment of God's plan despite human opposition?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Acts 4:27-28 depicts God’s sovereign control over events, even those intended for harm, fulfilling His divine counsel.

questions.question: What theological significance does Barnabas’ act in Acts 4:37 have in the context of early church teaching on stewardship?
options: It exemplifies voluntary generous giving as an act of faith and unity
It shows compulsory sacrifice imposed by leaders
It prioritizes personal wealth over communal needs
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies voluntary generous giving as an act of faith and unity
questions.explanation: Acts 4:37 describes Barnabas selling land and giving the proceeds to the apostles, illustrating voluntary generosity.

questions.question: How does Acts 4:17-18 demonstrate the early church's conflict with religious authorities over gospel proclamation?
options: It shows authorities forbidding teaching in Jesus' name to suppress the gospel
It shows authorities encouraging gospel teaching
It depicts harmony between church and religious leaders
It describes religious leaders joining the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: It shows authorities forbidding teaching in Jesus' name to suppress the gospel
questions.explanation: Acts 4:17-18 records the council commanding apostles not to speak or teach in Jesus' name, evidencing opposition to the gospel.
